reviews.author: Pawel Z.

reviews.title: Great keyboard for rapid trigger, more budget friendly vs the wooting 80he
reviews.comment:
Coming from a wooting 80he, this is good. I had to return my wooting because the rapid trigger would make buttons stopped working, I even had another one sent to me and still same issues, could be my hardware I have no idea, so looking for a replacement I’ve choose this one over the razer which is a big competitor and mostly choose Logitech to stay in the ecosystem because I have a super light 2 mouse.
This review will be compared to the wooting 80 he which is the best keyboard in the market.
The wooting keys feel way better and the sound clicks are much better too. Coming to Logitech is a huge difference I wish the sound of clicks were more dreamy like wooting also wish the buttons are softer
Software to me is all the same on both of them. Wooting probably has a slight edge but not by much. Wooting has more rgb lights and it sticks out more if you care for that.
Rapid trigger works excellent and it feels like I’m moving faster on games on cs2/valorant the respond time Is amazing the upgrade to a rapid trigger keyboard is worth it for that alone.
This keyboard has a volume knob which is big to me and wooting doesn’t.
Overall if the wooting was able to work on my computer I’ve give it a 5/5 and this Logitech keyboard 4.5/5 for the price
I got this brand new on sale $150 which imo should be the retail price, I wouldn’t pay $190 might as well spend more on a wooting.
My honest non sponsored review.
reviews.author: Yah

reviews.title: Great keyboard except for one major issue
reviews.comment: Great keyboard, very smooth and solid feel to the actual typing. Really feels built to last, and the texture is pleasant to the touch. It's not slick like uncoated keyboard keys. One thing that's annoying, though, is this keyboard has a tendency to disconnect, and unplugging it and replugging it in doesn't seem to help matters. The only thing that fixes this is a full PC reboot, which is time consuming and annoying. I hope they fix this. It'd be one thing if it were a bluetooth issue but this is a *wired* keyboard, so it makes even less sense.

reviews.title: Innovative Hall-Effect Analog/Linear Mechanical Switch Keyboard
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/F1CCS4XuQyL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/81IFba4Pj2L._SY256.jpg Typing experience was amazing. The key press feels noticeably smoother and faster than Cherry MX Brown Switch as well as Cherry MX Blue and Cherry MX Red Switches. You can customize rapid trigger, key actuation point, as well as Lightsync RGB lighting, Button mapping, etc. via Logitech G Hub software.
Only side is that it does not come with numpads since this is TKL (Ten Keyless) version which was why it was specifically designed for competitive eSport players to compete other players during tournament. But since I'm not pro tournament gamer, I just want to use this keyboard for typing, gaming, and professional productivity work such as animation and sketches. In addition, it doesn't come with Lightspeed Wireless technology which is a bummer. Not only that, but it also doesn't come with carry pouch to transport for vacation on flight.
Yes, it comes with USB C to USB A Cable to connect from your keyboard to your computer.
Other than that, the Hall-Effect mechanical switches were very impressive and innovative to address actuation key presses, and also ideal to improve gameplay responsiveness and especially input lag, regardless game engine title.
P.S. if you need numpads, you can purchase numpads from 3rd party vendors which they sell wide variety of key numpads on the market which may cost roughly between $15-$25 before sales tax.
